content: 1. The coadministration of fedratinib, a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP2C19, with dual inhibitors of these enzymes should be avoided or replaced with an alternative drug. The effects of such coadministration have not been studied. 2. Dexlansoprazole reduces the levels or effects of ferric carboxymaltose by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Close monitoring is recommended. 3. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of ferric gluconate, ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 4. Fexinidazole increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is significant, and alternative drugs should be considered. Coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects associated with CYP3A4 substrates. 5. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as coadministration with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of flibanserin-related adverse effects. 6. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 7. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 8. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid coadministration with proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) if possible. If PPI treatment is necessary, separate gefitinib and PPI doses by 12 hours. 9. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A substrates. Alternative drugs should be considered. 10. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of indinavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of infigratinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of iron dextran complex and iron sucrose by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 13. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 14. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 15. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole and ketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 17. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir by increasing gastric pH. Proton pump inhibitor doses comparable to omeprazole <20 mg can be administered simultaneously with ledipasvir/sofosbuvir under fasted conditions. Close monitoring is recommended. 18. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of lemborexant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. A lower nightly dose of lemborexant is recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage modifications. 19. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrates initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 20. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of levoketoconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 21. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of levothyroxine, liothyronine, and liotrix by increasing gastric pH. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Conflicting evidence exists regarding these interactions. Close monitoring is recommended. 22. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of lisdexamfetamine by reducing gastric acidity, which decreases the time to maximum concentration (Tmax) for amphetamine and dextroamphetamine. The area under the curve (AUC) remains unaffected. 23. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by affecting CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the dose of lonafarnib or continue at the starting dose. 24. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 25. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, as it may result in heart failure due to systolic dysfunction. 26. Dexlansoprazole decreases the effects of mesalamine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to sustained-release dosage forms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels of methotrexate by decreasing renal clearance, increasing the risk of toxicity at higher doses. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Dexlansoprazole decreases the effects of methylphenidate by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Dexlansoprazole increases the levels or effects of midazolam intranasal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended, as coadministration may prolong sedation. 30. Mitotane decreases the levels of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 31. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies to mycophenolate mofetil but is less significant for enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium formulations. 32. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of nelfinavir by an unspecified mechanism, potentially leading to virologic failure and resistance. This interaction is contraindicated. 33. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels or effects of neratinib, nilotinib, pazopanib, and pexidartinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid or use alternative drugs. For pexidartinib, consider using H2-receptor antagonists or antacids instead of PPIs. 34. Phenobarbital and phenytoin decrease the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of phytoestrogens and polysaccharide iron by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Close monitoring is recommended. 36. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of ponatinib by increasing gastric pH. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 37. Posaconazole increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, while dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 38. Primidone decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. 39. Ribociclib increases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 40. Rifampin and rifapentine decrease the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Dexlansoprazole decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH, potentially leading to treatment failure. This interaction is contraindicated.
